title: Approximating High-Dimensional Earth Mover's Distance as Fast as Closest Pair
authors: Lorenzo Beretta (IBM Research, USA), Vincent Cohen-Addad (Google Research, USA), Rajesh Jayaram (Google Research, USA), Erik Waingarten (University of Pennsylvania, USA)
abstract: We give a reduction from $(1+\eps)$-approximate Earth Mover's Distance (EMD) to $(1+\epsilon)$-approximate Closest Pair (CP). As a consequence, we improve the fastest known approximation algorithm for high-dimensional EMD. Here, given $p\in [1, 2]$ and two sets of $n$ points $X%, Y \subset (\R^d,\ell_p)$, their EMD is the minimum cost of a perfect matching between $X$ and $Y$, where the cost of matching two vectors is their ℓ_p distance. Further, CP is the basic problem of finding a pair of points realizing $\min_{x \in X, y\in Y} ||x-y||_p$. Our contribution is twofold: (i) We show that if a $(1+\epsilon)$-approximate CP can be computed in time $n^{2-\phi}$, then a $1+O(\epsilon)$ approximation to EMD can be computed in time $n^{2-\Omega(\phi)}$; (ii) Plugging in the fastest known algorithm for CP, we obtain a $(1+\epsilon)$-approximation algorithm for EMD running in time $n^{2-\tilde{\Omega}(\epsilon^{1/3})}$ for high-dimensional point sets, which improves over the prior fastest running time of $n^{2-\Omega(\eps^2)}$. Our main technical contribution is a sublinear implementation of the Multiplicative Weights Update framework for EMD. Specifically, we demonstrate that the updates can be executed without ever explicitly computing or storing the weights; instead, we exploit the underlying geometric structure to perform the updates implicitly.
